spans.s:
उल्का उल्का, f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. उष्), a fiery
phenomenon in the sky, a meteor, fire falling from
heaven; a firebrand; torch; fire, a flame, title of a
grammar; [cf. Cambro-Brit. ulw, ‘ashes.’]
—उल्का-
जिह्व, अस्, m., N. of a Rakṣas.
—उल्का-धारिन्, ई,
[]
इणी, इ, a torch-bearer.
—उल्का-पात, अस्, m. the fall
of a meteor.
—उल्का-मालिन्, ई, m., N. of one of Śiva's
attendants.
—उल्का-मुख, अस्, m. a demon or
goblin (with a face or mouth of fire who eats what is
vomited, having been a negligent Brāhman in his
lifetime); N. of a descendant of Ikṣvāku; (ई), f.
a fox.

उल्कुषी, f. a fiery phenomenon in the sky, a
meteor; firebrand.
—उल्कुषी-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved.
accompanied by fiery phenomena.
